clue.text: Consuming about a stone, I'm guessing

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the eating word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: consuming food is eating it
ST is the standard abbreviation for stone, the weight
I'm contracts to IM once the apostrophe is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into a hefty meal, roughly a stone of it, they reckon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means going round here, not 'approximately', which the surface wants it to mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimating is judging a quantity roughly, which is educated guessing.

parts.note: a sound that bounces back off a wall and is heard again, rather than a jilted lover or a ball taken off the backboard

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests romance or ball games; what really comes back off a surface is a reflected sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound returning to the listener is heard as it rebounds.

clue.text: Skilful support for a number of commandments can be defended

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: there are ten commandments in the Bible
skilful means able

explanation.surface: Praise for someone clever enough to prop up the Ten Commandments, a defensible position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for' puts ABLE under TEN in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or maintained against attack.

parts.note: read as wearing a suit tailored to one's own body, not merely being especially well matched

explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' looks like 'appropriate'; it means dressed in a suit cut for the wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothing is cut to fit a particular person, so its wearer is specially suited.

parts.note: something understood without being said is tacit
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: An unspoken pot kept back for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little, so is reserved in manner.

clue.text: Railwaymen once came to Kent for tender

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, since merged into another union
Kent is a county in south-east England, so SE

explanation.surface: Former rail-union members travelled down to Kent to make an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like a bid; here it is a verb, to care for.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient or child is to look after them, as a carer does.

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow is to check or stop it
the main stalk of a plant

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to halt a flow, and the stalk bearing leaves and flowers.

indicators.note: to sort something can mean to rearrange it, so these letters get reordered

explanation.surface: A hesitant description of mild dalliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges FLIRTED; the whole clue also defines, since toying with someone is a kind of flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: Toying with someone's affections is a light form of romantic dalliance.

clue.text: Tom remains puzzled by economic theory

indicators.note: puzzled letters are confused and jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom is left baffled by a theory of economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetarism is the economic doctrine that controlling the money supply controls inflation.

clue.text: Added an edge in phone discussion

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone sharpened their argument during a phone conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpening a blade on a whetstone gives it a keen edge.

definitions.meaning: Fletcher ... led the mutiny on the Bounty

explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher Christian was the 18th-century mutineer on HMS Bounty.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Bounty mutineer is also the word for a believer in Jesus.

parts.note: being quits means being even, all square
knocking is bashing

explanation.surface: Giving up knocking the soldiers' parade practice.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for parade-ground drill, done on the barrack square.

clue.text: Face unpleasant task, and grab the lead?

definitions.meaning: to steel oneself to do something hard
literally to clamp one's teeth on a lead slug, as wounded soldiers once did

explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests leash or first place; it is the metal of a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from patients biting on a bullet during surgery without anaesthetic.

parts.note: to allude to something is to refer to it
the end is the result
um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A ballot that hints at a conclusion, delivered with a stammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a national ballot on a single question.

clue.text: Always, a saint is for good

parts.note: ever means always
Sir Thomas More was canonised as a saint

explanation.surface: A declaration that a saint remains forever devoted to virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas More, Henry VIII's executed chancellor, is Saint Thomas More.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean permanently, for all time.

clue.text: Pictures returned to the German dealer

indicators.note: returned means the word for pictures goes back to front

parts.note: pictures are art
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Paintings sent back to a German merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, as a merchant does.

clue.text: Indication by the way to finalise outgoing letters

parts.note: to finalise a contract is to sign it
the post is mail sent out

explanation.surface: A remark in passing about completing the outgoing mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like an aside; it means beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside post with arms points travellers towards places.

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are messed about into another order

explanation.surface: Fooling a foolish mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone into a situation is to snare them.

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange drinking toast raised to the thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the Chinese thinker Laozi's Way are adherents of a philosophy and religion.

clue.text: Mature deer worth a lot in America?

parts.note: grown-up, big
bucks are male deer

explanation.surface: Fully grown stags fetching a high price in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: In US slang a buck is a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a large sum of money.

parts.note: CA is chartered accountant, so the possessive gives CAS
a model who posed sat for an artist
a means one

explanation.surface: An accountant modelled for a portrait holding a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian dessert of layered ice cream with candied fruit.

parts.note: people who hold that species arise through natural selection, not people who naturally believe in choosing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Naturally' looks like 'of course'; it pairs with 'selection' to make Darwin's natural selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of Darwinian theory hold that natural selection shapes species.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wrap-up offering a few closing lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sums up totals or overall conclusions.

parts.note: read as what belongs to Len Hutton the England cricket captain, possessive and all, and also as an optical device

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Len Hutton was an England cricket captain of the 1950s; his first name with the possessive spells out a piece of optics.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved glass bends light to bring an image into sharp detail.

indicators.note: appalling suggests something dreadful done to the letters, which are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless driver doing a shocking speed on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' is the anagram signal; the 's after 'man' stands for 'is' and is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold outlaw who acts without regard for danger.

clue.text: Picture that's making cover of periodical

indicators.note: making a cover of something means wrapping round it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
a mag is a magazine

explanation.surface: An illustration chosen for a magazine's front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' gives the Latin abbreviation i.e., id est; 'making cover of' says it wraps round the periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual representation such as a photograph.

indicators.note: after puts the request piece following the minute piece

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for minute
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A moment later, someone asks for their cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean disguise or conceal.

clue.text: Two items for dinner table are in the window

parts.note: a plate and a drinking glass both sit on a laid table
the second item, a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: Tableware displayed in a shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: Large sheets of thick polished glass are used for shop windows.
